extracted.intended_audience: school and university administrators, Title IX coordinators, legal counsel, policymakers, and stakeholders who submitted or read comments on the Title IX NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Preamble discussion and Department responses to public comments on the Title IX NPRM, describing scope, applicability, enforcement, evidentiary basis, and procedural limits of the final regulations. Intended to explain how the final rule will be interpreted and applied by recipients and OCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rulemaking (NPRM subjects only)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The scope of matters addressed by the final regulations is defined by the subjects presented in the NPRM. Therefore, the Department declines to address other topics outside of this original scope, such as pregnancy, parenting, or athletics under Title IX, coverage of Title IX to fraternities and sororities, whether speech codes discriminate based on sex, funding intended to protect women or young adults on campus, funding cuts to girls' programs by recipients, or forms of harassment other than sexual harassment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an issue was not presented in the NPRM, the Department declines to address it in the final rule; inquiries about application of Title IX to particular organizations may be referred to the organization's Title IX Coordinator or to the Assistant Secretary as indicated in §106.8(b)(1); complaints alleging sex discrimination that does not constitute sexual harassment may be handled under the equitable grievance procedures recipients must adopt under §106.8(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of §§106.44 and 106.45 limited to Title IX sexual harassment
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Department ... clarif[ies] that the response obligations in §106.44 and the grievance process in §106.45 apply only to allegations of Title IX sexual harassment; the final regulations impose no new obligations or requirements with respect to non-Title IX sexual harassment and do not alter existing regulations under civil rights laws such as Title VI ... or regulations under disability laws such as IDEA, Section 504, or ADA."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must continue to comply with all other applicable civil-rights and disability statutes and their implementing regulations; the final rule does not change obligations under other federal laws and OCR/the Department will continue to enforce those laws separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of 'complainant' and 'respondent' are not limited to students or employees
rubrics_metrics.description: "The definitions of 'complainant' and 'respondent' do not restrict either party to being a student or employee, and, therefore, the final regulations do apply to allegations that an employee was sexually harassed by a student."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Department declined to substitute the term 'member' for 'student'/'employee', the regulatory definitions make clear parties are not limited to those labels — the rules can apply to employee-victim situations involving students, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of the terms 'students' and 'employees' (no change to 'members')
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Department declines to change the words 'students' and 'employees' to 'members' in the final regulations, because doing so could create inconsistencies with the current regulations, and the meaning of the term 'member' is not readily understood by reference to other State and Federal laws, in the way that 'employee' is."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology was retained to avoid legal ambiguity and inconsistency with other state and federal law references; this is a deliberate drafting choice rather than an expansion or limitation of who may be a complainant/respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement authority and non-retroactivity of final regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Department agrees ... administrative enforcement of Title IX obligations is vital ... and the Department will vigorously enforce the final regulations. Nothing in these final regulations alters the existing statutory and regulatory framework under which the Department exercises its administrative authority to take enforcement actions against recipients for non-compliance with Title IX including the circumstances under which a recipient's Federal financial assistance may be terminated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will enforce prospectively and will not enforce the final regulations retroactively; whether prospective enforcement affects existing resolution agreements requires case-by-case examination and the Department will provide technical assistance regarding enforceability of existing agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Department authority over private rights of action and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Department does not have authority or ability to affect the existence of judicially-implied private rights of action under Title IX or the remedies available through such private lawsuits."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that the Department eliminate private rights of action or bar payment of attorney fees/damages/costs cannot be implemented via this rulemaking because they fall outside the Department's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to OCR's Case Processing Manual are outside rulemaking scope
rubrics_metrics.description: "Changes to OCR's Case Processing Manual are outside the scope of this rulemaking process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenter proposals to revise OCR's Case Processing Manual (e.g., eliminate biases, protect undocumented students from deportation risk when filing, alter 180-day timeliness) are not addressed through this rulemaking; such operational/process changes require separate action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-substantive comments and symbolic submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: "For comments submitted with no substantive text, names of survivor advocacy organizations, or pictures or graphics depicting, e.g., feminist icons, protest marches ... the Department has considered the viewpoints that such pictures, graphics, and slogans appear to convey."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even submissions lacking textual substance were considered for the viewpoint they conveyed; agencies will note and account for collective expressions (images, slogans, organization names) when summarizing public input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of empirical evidence and cited literature to inform the rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Many commenters urged the Department to consult literature concerning the prevalence and impact of sexual harassment ... The Department has considered the sources cited to by commenters. For reasons described in this preamble, the Department believes that the final regulations create a predictable framework governing recipients' responses to allegations of sexual harassment in furtherance of Title IX's non-discrimination mandate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department reviewed a wide body of empirical studies and reports (listed in the preamble) about prevalence, impacts, reporting rates, institutional dynamics, and consequences; that evidence informed the Department's conclusion that these regulations will provide clarity and accountability to restore or preserve complainants' equal access to education when harassment constitutes sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability requirement when harassment constitutes sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: "When sexual harassment constitutes sex discrimination covered by Title IX, the final regulations hold schools accountable for responding in ways that restore or preserve a complainant's equal access to education."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This accountability standard is applied across elementary/secondary and postsecondary institutions when facts meet the Title IX sexual harassment definition — institutions must respond under the final regulations to restore or preserve equal educational access.
